notes: 2026-07-28 is a Tuesday. This case is about DATES: one relative, one conditional, one deliberately unresolvable.

items.label: relative-date-end-of-week
items.anchor: I want to get it merged by end of week
items.why: 'by end of week' has to be resolved against the meeting date. Tuesday 2026-07-28 -> Friday 2026-07-31. A model that returns null here is under-confident; one that returns a date in the wrong week has anchored on today rather than the meeting.

items.label: relative-date-first-thing-monday
items.anchor: I'll fix the staging deploy and have it green first thing Monday
items.why: 'first thing Monday' is the NEXT Monday after a Tuesday meeting, which crosses a month boundary — 2026-08-03, not 2026-07-27. Also a reversal: Tomasz declines the work once before committing, so the model must score the second statement and not the first.

items.label: conditional-commitment
items.anchor: I'll ship the retry logic on Thursday
items.why: Hedged on a vendor dependency, but still a commitment with a named owner and a stated day. Dropping it because of the 'assuming' clause is a recall failure; a real reviewer wants to see it.

items.label: unconditional-side-commitment
items.description: Chase the vendor for the sandbox key
items.anchor: But I'll chase them either way
items.why: Sits inside a discussion about what happens if a dependency slips, which is why it is easy to read as hedging rather than as work. It is not hedged: 'either way' makes it unconditional. A second, smaller commitment buried in the answer to a question about a first one.

items.label: unresolvable-date
items.description: Write up the incident from last Tuesday
items.why: A real commitment with a genuinely unknowable date — 'when I get a chance', said in as many words. due_date MUST be null. Inventing one here is the quiet failure mode: a fabricated deadline propagates into a task system and someone is chased for a date nobody agreed to.

must_not_extract.label: trap-someday-refactor
must_not_extract.anchor: We might want to refactor the whole connector layer at some point
must_not_extract.why: 'might want to' plus 'at some point'. An idea wearing engineering clothes.

must_not_extract.label: trap-declined-then-superseded
must_not_extract.anchor: I could take a look at it sometime this week if nobody else is on it
must_not_extract.why: 'I could ... if nobody else is' is not a commitment, and it is superseded two lines later by a real one. Emitting BOTH this and the Monday commitment double-counts one piece of work. Only the later, firm statement is the action item.

must_not_extract.label: trap-question-status
must_not_extract.anchor: Is anyone actually looking at that
must_not_extract.why: A question. Reads urgent, commits nobody.

must_not_extract.label: trap-observation-metrics
must_not_extract.anchor: The error rates on the webhook endpoint have doubled this month
must_not_extract.why: An observation, and one the speaker immediately downgrades to 'still tiny'. Nobody agreed to do anything.

must_not_extract.label: trap-unowned-should
must_not_extract.anchor: Someone should write up the incident from last Tuesday
must_not_extract.why: Unowned when voiced; becomes an item only when Elena claims it. Counted once, against Elena.

label_corrections: The 'chase the vendor' item was added after the FIRST run of this harness flagged it as a false positive. It was not — "But I'll chase them either way" is the prompt's own canonical commitment form, stated unconditionally by a named person. I had written the line as colour for the conditional-commitment case and failed to label it. Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because a fixture edited to raise a score deserves suspicion.
